name: vector_table

name: main
note: flash 0xA0CC; reset handler ends with `ldr r0,=0xa0cd; bx r0`

name: default_handler_stubs

name: save_cfg_if_changed

name: init_chip_uid

name: iap_read_uid

name: iap_entry_call

name: iap_prepare_sectors
note: IAP 50 (0x32); r0 = start sector, r1 = end sector; cclk word 100000 kHz

name: iap_erase_sectors
note: IAP 52 (0x34); same args as prepare

name: iap_copy_ram_to_flash
note: IAP 51 (0x33); r0 = flash dest, r1 = RAM src, r2 = size; returns 1 if status 0

name: iap_blank_check

name: iap_compare

name: wdt_feed_raw

name: wdt_set_timeout_ms

name: wdt_stop_feeding
note: sets 0x100005d5 = 1; watchdog then expires = chip reset

name: flash_cfg_write

name: flash_cfg_read

name: write_loader_marker

name: cfg9_write_0

name: cfg9_write_20

name: cfg7_write_0

name: cfg8_write_20

name: cfg_read_main
note: flash_cfg_read(sector 9, offset 0x32, dst, len); write twin 0x159fa

name: flash_sector_addr
note: LPC176x sector start addresses: 22 words, 0x0000..0xF000 step 0x1000 then 0x10000, 0x18000, 0x20000, 0x28000, 0x30000, 0x38000

name: flash_log_append
note: appends text lines to a RAM buffer then to flash sectors 19-21 (0x13..0x15); no BL callers and no table pointer found (purpose unknown)

name: duml_reply_build
note: called as (frame, payload, len, scratch) before 0x27de; builds the response frame

name: duml_reply_send
note: sends the frame built by 0x2832

name: duml_local_dispatch
note: switch on cmd_set (frame[9]) via TBB at 0x53d4, indexes 0-9; set 0 = general, set 9 -> 0x56e4

name: duml_route
note: receiver type = frame[5] & 0x1f: 0x0E and 0x14 -> local (0x5be2 -> 0x53c8); 0 -> rewritten to 0x0E, local; 0x1F -> local + forward; other types forwarded to a port by TBB at 0x5c8c

name: duml_enter_loader
note: set 0 cmd 0x07; payload[0] must be 0; rx 0x14: 0xd71e, wait, 0xe000 (FPGA); else 0x158b0 marker write. status 0 or 0xF6. After reply, rx 0x0E and status 0: 0x254, WDT 100 ms, stop feeding, spin = watchdog reset

name: duml_update_confirm
note: set 0 cmd 0x08; rx 0x14 only: reply [status from 0xe0d8, 0x0200]

name: duml_update_finish
note: set 0 cmd 0x0A; rx 0x14 only, payload[0] == 0: 0xe0f4(payload+1); status 4 -> reply 0; 6 -> 0xF2 then reset pulse; else 0xFF then reset pulse (P1.23 low, 2 units, high, 200 units, rerun 0xde96)

name: duml_reboot_chip
note: set 0 cmd 0x0B; rx 0x0E only; payload[1] must be 0 or 1 (else 0xE3); after reply: 0x17352, feed, 0x254, WDT timeout = u32 at payload+2, stop feeding

name: duml_get_device_state
note: set 0 cmd 0x0C; rx 0x0E/0x14; payload[0]>>4 must be 0 (else 0xE3); reply [0,0, u32]; u32 = RAM 0x1000034c for rx 0x14, else 0

name: duml_set_device_version
note: set 0 cmd 0x0D; rx 0x0E only; writes 16 payload bytes to flash sector 9 offset 0 (0x9000); status 0xF4 on failure; reply [status, 0, 16 B read back]

name: duml_get_device_version
note: set 0 cmd 0x01; rx 0x14: u32 words RAM 0x10000344 (FPGA id word) and 0x10000348 if 0xbdc4 != 0, else 0xFFFFFFFE; rx 0x0E: words from 0x10007f70/74 handoff pair and RAM 0x10000000/6/8

name: duml_query_device_info
note: set 0 cmd 0xFF; reply carries string at 0x4bb8; no chip ID

name: duml_set0_cmd30
note: set 0 cmd 0x30, sub-commands 1-4 on payload[0]: 1->0x4e3e/0x4f02, 2->0x4dc2 (unconditional), 3->0x4924/0x4b7c, 4->0x48a8 (unconditional); subs 1 and 3 pick between the two addresses by board_strap_code (0x10000006); sub bodies not traced further

name: duml_set0_cmd32
note: set 0 cmd 0x32, sub-commands 1-3; reads RAM 0x10000021 / 0x10002760; not decoded

name: duml_set9_dispatch
note: reached from set 9 (TBB idx 9 at 0x53d4); switch on cmd_id: 0x0C -> 0x2bca (Master Id set), 0x0D -> 0x2b10 (get), 0x10/0x12/0x13/0x14/0x15 -> 0x2adc/0x2a6c/0x29b4/0x28c2/0x27c2, 0x2C -> 0xba1c

name: duml_set9_cmd2c_keyed
note: switch on u16 key at frame+0xd: 0x901 -> 0xb6fc, 0x902 -> 0xb750, 0x903 -> 0xb7c4 (save cfg, WDT reboot), 0x904 -> 0xb820, 0x911 -> 0xb86c, 0x912 -> 0xb8b8, 0x913 -> 0xb906, 0x914 -> 0xb99e

name: reply_chip_uid_0904
note: reply key = req key + 0x50 (0x954); payload = 16 bytes from RAM 0x100005d8 (LPC1765 IAP serial number), frame length 0x18

name: cmd_0903_save_and_reboot
note: calls 0x254, WDT 100 ms, stop feeding, replies; second reboot route besides Reboot Chip

name: spi0_xfer_byte
note: legacy SPI0 at 0x40020000: write S0SPDR, poll S0SPSR bit7 (SPIF), read back; IRQs off during write

name: spi0_init
note: r0 = clock 4,000,000 (0x3d0900, from caller 0xbdca); S0SPCR 0x82c (8 bit, master, CPHA=1, CPOL=0); pins P0.15 SCK, P0.17 MISO, P0.18 MOSI via PINSEL0/1; divider search in steps of 2 from 8

name: spi_fpga_init
note: PINSEL4 bits 19:18 cleared (P2.9 = GPIO), FIO2DIR bit9 out (CS), spi0_init(4 MHz), CS high, RAM 0x10000313 = 3

name: get_fpga_mode
note: returns byte at RAM 0x10000313 (0, 1 or 3 seen in callers; selects script table)

name: fpga_reg_write
note: CS (P2.9, FIO2CLR 0x200) low, bytes [0x0E, reg, val] (args r0=0x0E, r1=reg, r2=val), CS high

name: fpga_reg_read
note: CS low, bytes [0x0F, reg, 0xFF], returns last byte, CS high

name: fpga_burst_write
note: [cmd, reg, n bytes] in one CS frame; no callers, no pointers

name: fpga_burst_read
note: [cmd, reg] then n x 0xFF in one CS frame; no callers, no pointers

name: ad936x_reg_write
note: FPGA [0E 01 01] arm; CS low; [0x80|addr>>8, addr&0xff, val]; CS high; FPGA [0E 01 (flag?02:00)]; same bridge as m0900 0x0800cebe

name: ad936x_reg_read
note: same bridge, read; same as m0900 0x0800cf00

name: fpga_script_exec_record
note: interprets a 4-byte script record, opcodes 5..12 via TBB; same role as m0900 0x0800d318

name: fpga_reg0_toggle
note: FPGA reg0 |= 1 then &= 0xfe; same as m0900 0x0800d7a4

name: fpga_post_boot_config
note: if mode 0/1: P1.23 low 10 units, high; runs FPGA/AD9363 record scripts (0x20310, 0x1d1d4, 0x23d68 by mode) through 0xba6c; returns nonzero on success

name: fpga_bits_set
note: record idx r0 of table 0x249b1: reg |= mask (read via 0xbe24, write via 0xbdf6)

name: fpga_bits_clear
note: reg &= ~mask

name: fpga_bits_test
note: returns reg & mask

name: fpga_read_id_word
note: reads FPGA regs 0x8B, 0x8C, 0x8D, 0x8E into a u32

name: fpga_boot_handshake
note: same sequence as m0900 0x0800cfd0, 3 tries; returns 4 = ready, 3/8/9 fail; stores id word to RAM 0x10000344

name: radio_quiesce
note: clears bit 3 of the port 2 falling-edge IRQ enable (0x400280b4), clears a state byte, resets Timer1 (0x40008004 = 2)

name: fpga_enter_upgrade_mode
note: boot-style handshake with the bit records, returns 0 ok / 5 / 8 / 9 fail; same role as m0900 0x0800d112

name: fpga_update_confirm
note: if RAM 0x10000344 != 0x010007ec set record 10; set record 1; returns 0

name: fpga_update_finish
note: needs reg 0x0F bit1 (else 7); if id word != 0x010007ec compares FPGA reg 0x09 with payload[0], reg 0x08 with payload[1] (else 6); then handshake records; returns 4 ok (also clears bit0 of [0x10000344+8]), 2/3/8/0xA handshake outcomes, 6 mismatch, 7 not in upgrade mode. Same role as m0900 0x0800d206

name: fpga_handshake_tail
note: tests record 5 in a retry loop; no callers

name: fpga_bit_records
note: 11 x [idx, reg, mask]: 0 r00 b0; 1 r01 0x20; 2 r0F 0x02; 3 r00 b0; 4 r01 b0; 5 r8A 0x03; 6 r01 0x10; 7 r0F b0; 8 r00 0x80; 9 r0F b0; 10 r02 b0. Byte-identical to m0900 0x0801623c

name: crc8_table
note: 256 B CRC-8 lookup (Dallas/Maxim style) used by 0xeb10

name: crc8_update
note: r0 = seed, r1 = data, r2 = len-1 count loop; table 0x249d2

name: crc8_update2
note: second CRC-8 routine, table 0x256b8, seed r2

name: crc16_update
note: CRC-16 table routine (args buf, len, seed), table at offset 0x254b8 (literal 0x2f4b8)

name: FpgaErr
note: no code xref found by this tool (ADR via other form)

name: rc_state
note: RC link state struct; 0x86 B saved to flash by 0x254

name: chip_uid_16
note: 16 B IAP serial number (4 words), written once by 0x396, sent by 0xb820

name: uid_check_bytes
note: 5 B derived from the UID (sum / CRC)

name: fpga_id_word
note: u32 read from FPGA regs 0x8B..0x8E at handshake; compared to 0x010007ec

name: wdt_nofeed
note: 0 = feed watchdog; 1 = stop feeding (reset)

name: iap_cmd_block
note: IAP command (+0x00..+0x10) and result (+0x14..) blocks; +0x28 = 0x200 B flash scratch

name: loader_handoff_pair
note: value / ~value pair read by Get Device Version (rx 0x0E); never written by the app (inferred: written by the bootloader above the stack top)

name: duml_set9_cmd0c_report
note: cmd_set 9, cmd_id 0x0C (APK SetConnectMaster); reads rc_state 0x100005e8+0x62/0x63/0x64/0x70/0x71-1/0x79, sends 15 B reply; despite the name this reads+reports, does not write

name: duml_set9_cmd0d_write_fields
note: cmd_set 9, cmd_id 0x0D (APK GetConnectMaster); parses payload as (field_id,value) pairs, writes each into rc_state+0x62/0x63/0x64/0x70/0x71/0x79; field 1 also sets 0x100000c8+0xc=1 if frame[4]&0x1f==9; unknown field -> status 0xE0. Despite the name this writes, does not report

name: duml_set9_cmd10_setmode
note: cmd_set 9, cmd_id 0x10 (APK GetSearchMode); writes payload[0] to RAM 0x100000c8+0xd; 1 B status reply

name: duml_set9_cmd12_multiset
note: cmd_set 9, cmd_id 0x12 (APK GetToggle); calls 5 small setters (0x17a94/178f0/17906/1791c/17978/17942) from payload bytes 0xb-0xe; those helpers not traced further

name: duml_set9_cmd13_slave_join_reply
note: cmd_set 9, cmd_id 0x13 (APK RequestSlaveJoin); no state write; builds 8 B capability reply (flag bit from 0x16848, 14-bit field from 0x179ec, 2 B from 0x179fc, 1 B from 0x17980, RAM 0x1000000c*10)

name: duml_set9_cmd14_slave_list
note: cmd_set 9, cmd_id 0x14 (APK GetSlaveList); dual-mode accessor on rc_state+0xf: mode 0/1 each move 1 B between payload and RAM 0x10000311/0x10000310 by receiver-type nibble (2 or 0xE), clamped vs 0x10000272; mode 1 also runs the DeleteSlave match-and-decrement below

name: duml_set9_cmd15_delete_slave
note: cmd_set 9, cmd_id 0x15 (APK DeleteSlave); if payload[0]==0 and frame[6:8] (u16) matches RAM 0x100000c8+0x9e, decrements slave-count byte at +0x9c (floor 0); RC-to-RC multi-controller link, not aircraft binding (docs/duml-protection.md)

name: rc_slave_state
note: second RC-link state struct (slave-join/list/delete fields: +0x9c count, +0x9e id, +0xc flag); distinct from rc_state 0x100005e8

name: boot_init
note: early boot routine (called from reset chain before main app init): clears GPIO1 DIR bits 21/24 (sets them input), reads board_strap_code from GPIO1 PIN, inits RTC, calls init_chip_uid (0x0396), inits UART0-3 (0x0798/0a5a/0d02/0fa6 offsets below), runs join/pairing setup

name: board_strap_code
note: 3-bit board/variant code = (GPIO1.27<<2)|(GPIO1.21<<1)|GPIO1.24, read once at boot_init (0x05b0); GPIO1 PIN reg 0x2009c034, DIR reg 0x2009c020; ground-side equivalent of m0900's PA0/PC15/PC14 board code

name: duml_get_device_version
note: (extends existing row) rx 0x0E path, non-0x14 case: if board_strap_code==3 and a "ready" flag (RAM 0x10000000) is set, reply packs a fixed 0x03,0x03 pair instead of the live strap_code/0x10000008 byte pair - board strap is echoed to the host in this reply

name: duml_set0_cmd30_sub1_a
note: cmd0x30 sub-command 1, board_strap_code!=3 path (or ready flag clear)

name: duml_set0_cmd30_sub1_b
note: cmd0x30 sub-command 1, board_strap_code==3 path

name: duml_set0_cmd30_sub2
note: cmd0x30 sub-command 2; checks a 4-byte magic "G\x03\x11\x07" against RAM rc_slave_state record and a helper 0x197a2 result; clears RAM bit 0x10000f00[-0x40]&0xbf on helper==0; not board-strap gated

name: duml_set0_cmd30_sub3_a
note: cmd0x30 sub-command 3, board_strap_code!=3 path; builds/queues a slave-join-style record (0x47,3,0x11,7 header) via helper 0x1f98a

name: duml_set0_cmd30_sub3_b
note: cmd0x30 sub-command 3, board_strap_code==3 path; same record-build, keyed additionally on request sub-type 0x8d/0x52

name: duml_set0_cmd30_sub4
note: cmd0x30 sub-command 4; not board-strap gated; body not traced

name: duml_set9_cmd00
note: cmd_set 9, cmd_id 0x00 (no entry in APK CmdIdType - DJI-internal/legacy, like cmd_id 0x2c); copies 0x43 B payload into a struct, compares 5 fields (offsets +0x26/+0x2d/+0x2f/+0x33/+0x3b) against a reference; on match, overwrites those 5 fields with new values from payload (+0x3e..+0x42) - password/credential-style check-then-replace

name: duml_set9_cmd04
note: cmd_set 9, cmd_id 0x04 (APK GetHardwareParams); despite the name, a SETTER: calls generic indexed param store (0xdb60) with fixed index 0x0e, value=payload[1]; same inversion pattern as 0x0c/0x0d

name: duml_set9_cmd05
note: cmd_set 9, cmd_id 0x05 (APK GetPushParams); calls generic indexed param read (0xdc30) with fixed index 0x0f, returns 1 B in the reply

name: duml_set9_cmd06
note: cmd_set 9, cmd_id 0x06 (APK SetMaster); generic indexed param store (0xdb60), index = payload u16 (0..1, 0xfe00-0xfeff, 0xfff6-0xfffe sentinel range), value = payload[2]

name: duml_set9_cmd07
note: cmd_set 9, cmd_id 0x07 (APK GetMaster); generic indexed param read (0xdc30), same index space as 0x4c94; returns 1 B

name: duml_set9_cmd09
note: cmd_set 9, cmd_id 0x09 (APK GetName); despite the name, only WRITES payload[0] into RAM (DAT_0000ce18+0xb) and acks status 0 - no data returned; another Set/Get inversion instance

name: hwparam_set
note: generic indexed hardware/RF-param setter keyed by a u16 index; sentinel indices 0xfff6-0xfffe write bit-packed fields of a config struct at RAM ptr DAT_00017cd8 (+0xc/+0x10/+0x85/+0xa8/+0x269/+0xac); index range 0xfe00-0xfeff and plain small indices forward to 0x15df6(0x0e,idx,val) under IRQ-disabled critical section

name: hwparam_get
note: paired getter for 0xdb60's index space; same sentinel/struct layout

name: radio_tick_record_tx
note: TIMER0 IRQ-flag-driven periodic radio status/telemetry record builder; feeds board_strap_code==1 into one packed field (else a fixed value) before sending via port-dispatch cmd 0xb0 (0x25d8); shares structure with 0x93f0

name: radio_tick_record_tx_2
note: second instance of the 0x2c7c pattern, also keyed on board_strap_code==1

name: radio_start
note: radio bring-up chain (SPI0/FPGA handshake etc, per docs/ground-upgrade-path.md); sets an RF/link config nibble (struct field, mask 0xfffff0ff) to 0x100 default, 0x300 if board_strap_code==1, or 0x200 if a separate ready/mode flag (RAM ptr DAT_000178d0) is set - board strap selects one of (at least) 3 RF profiles here, the m1400 analogue of m0900's board-code-gated FPGA bring-up

name: port_send
note: frame-forward dispatcher, switch on port 0-5: 0=host/ACK ring buffer via 0x1f5e0 (OS critical-section wrapped); 1=chunked queue, almost certainly the Lightbridge radio TX path; 2=UART3 (0x21126); 3=UART0 (0x2091c); 4=UART1 (0x20bec); 5=CAN1/CAN2 (0x1bc08) - ground-side DUML relay bus, same architectural role as air-side CAN1/CAN2 (dataflow.md Sec 7.10)

name: duml_route_port_table
note: tbb inside duml_route, keyed by receiver-type (frame[5]&0x1f, 32 entries): 0x00->local (rewritten 0x0e); 0x0a->port0; 0x02/0x0d/0x10/0x16->port2; 0x18->port4; 0x19/0x1c->port5; 0x1f->local+conditional port0; 0x06/0x0e/0x14/0x1a/0x1b/0x1d/0x1e->no-op (0x0e/0x14 already intercepted earlier as local, per existing doc); all other values (majority)->port1

name: duml_set6_cmd40
note: cmd_set 6, cmd_id 0x40 (resolves the open "set 6" cross-reference in docs/ground-upgrade-path.md and docs/cpu-reversing-proof.md - genuinely a separate, smaller dispatch from cmd_set 9, reached from a frame[9]==6 special case at duml_route offset 0x5c76); stores a payload value to RAM and a 1-byte flag (payload[0x12]==0x0a -> 1, ==0xff -> no-op/return, else -> 0); role of the flag not traced further

name: os_pendsv_handler
note: PendSV vector (14) handler, NOT a dead stub: textbook uC/OS-III Cortex-M3 context switch (disable IRQ, save r4-r11 to OSTCBCurPtr-equivalent RAM 0x100004e4's stack via PSP, call a task-switch-hook function pointer, swap OSPrioCur/OSTCBCurPtr-equivalents at RAM 0x100004b0/0x100004e0 from the HighRdy pair at 0x100004b1/0x100004e4, restore r4-r11, msr psp, orr lr,#4, bx lr) - overturns the "bare-metal, no RTOS" assumption for this chip

name: os_systick_handler
note: SysTick vector (15) handler, also not a dead stub: calls two sub-functions (0x1dcc8 then 0x1e198) consistent with uC/OS-III's tick-ISR template (critical-section enter, OSTimeTick, critical-section exit)

name: os_critical_enter
note: CPU_SR-save-style critical-section entry, called from the SysTick handler and from port_send's port-0 path (0x1f5e0); paired with os_critical_exit

name: os_critical_exit
note: paired critical-section exit for os_critical_enter

name: rtos_fingerprint
note: uC/OS-III Idle Task (0x1238c), "Task Q"/"Task Sem" (0x123e4/0x123ec), "uC/OS-III Tick Task" (0x13ae0) - same RTOS fingerprint method already used to ID m0306 as uC/OS-III; confirms the PendSV/SysTick disassembly finding (0x19b46/0x12914) by a second, independent method
